title: Images
tagline: Swap your shapes for actual pictures.
whenToUse: Any time after Lesson 4. It works well between Lessons 4 and 5, or between 7 and 8 when you are starting to make your world look polished. One period, standalone.
builtOn: Lesson 2 (`extends Blob`) and Lesson 4 (control). Nothing after this depends on it.
goals: Add image files to a sketch using the `data/` folder
Show an image as a sprite using `ImageSprite`
Put a `PImage` inside your own `extends Blob` character so collisions still work
Explain the difference between `ImageSprite` (for decoration) and an image inside a Blob (for the player)

vocab.def: a special folder inside your sketch folder where Processing looks for images and sounds
a sprite from the library that shows an image file instead of a shape
Processing's type for a loaded image. Think of it as a variable that holds a picture
the command that reads an image file out of the `data/` folder
the see-through part of a PNG. Without it your character comes with a rectangle stuck to it

warmup: Have you played a game where the characters are pictures instead of shapes? Which one? Do you think that is hard to make happen?

howItWorks.h: The data folder is where Processing looks
p: Processing will not find your image unless it is in exactly the right place: a folder called `data` inside your sketch folder.
**Sketch → Show Sketch Folder.** Make a folder called `data` (exactly that, lowercase). Drag your image in. Done — Processing finds it automatically.
PNG, JPG, and GIF all work. **PNG is the one you want**, because it can have a transparent background.
`ImageSprite` shows a picture and has all the sprite methods you already know: `move()`, `setVelocity()`, `followMouse()`, `drawSprite()`.

code.label: Three ways to size an ImageSprite
code.body:
new ImageSprite(this, x, y, "tree.png")            // 100 x 100 pixels
new ImageSprite(this, x, y, "tree.png", 80)        // 80 x 80 square
new ImageSprite(this, x, y, "tree.png", 120, 80)   // 120 wide, 80 tall

bullets: **But it has no `collidesWith()`.** `ImageSprite` is not a `Blob`, so it cannot collide. Use it for scenery, not for things the player has to touch.

howItWorks.h: For your player, put the image inside a Blob
p: Your player needs collisions. So instead of using `ImageSprite`, you keep `extends Blob` — exactly what you wrote in Lesson 2 — and just change `drawSprite()` to draw a picture instead of shapes.

code.label: Same class, different drawing

bullets: `imageMode(CENTER)` makes the image measure from its middle, matching how `pos.x`/`pos.y` work. Without it, your art sits down and to the right of your hitbox.
`pushStyle()` and `popStyle()` save and restore Processing's settings so `imageMode` does not leak out and affect everything else you draw.
The radius in `super(...)` is **still** your hitbox. The picture does not change that.

howItWorks.h: The two rules, side by side
bullets: Needs to **collide** (player, collectibles, hazards)? → `extends Blob` with a `PImage` inside.
Just needs to **look nice** (trees, background, clouds)? → `ImageSprite`.

howItWorks.h: Why your image has a white box around it
p: Because the PNG was saved without transparency. The image really is a rectangle — the background just happens to be white.
Fix it by finding or making a PNG that has a transparent background. Free tools like remove.bg will strip a background for you.

steps: Find or draw a small PNG image for your character. A transparent background looks best. Free art: opengameart.org. Or draw a 32×32 character in any paint program.
Open your sketch and choose **Sketch → Show Sketch Folder**.
Make a new folder in there called `data` — exactly that, all lowercase.
Drag your image file into `data/`. Note the file name exactly, including capitals and the extension.
**Start with the easy one.** In your main sketch, add an `ImageSprite` decoration and draw it in `draw()`. Run it.
If you get a blank or colored box: the file name does not match, the file is not in `data/`, or the PNG has no transparency.
Adjust the size numbers until the proportions look right for your art.
**Now do your character.** Make a new tab called `MyImageCharacter` and paste in the class below.
In your main sketch, create a `MyImageCharacter` instead of a `MyCharacter`. Run it and move it around.
Tune the radius in `super(...)` so the collisions feel fair — slightly smaller than the picture usually feels best.

code.label: Main sketch tab
New tab — MyImageCharacter.pde

makeItYours: Find or draw your own character image. A PNG with a transparent background looks best by a mile.
Add a **background image**: `ImageSprite bg = new ImageSprite(this, width/2, height/2, "background.png", width, height);` drawn first in `draw()`.
Adjust the display size (the `60, 60` in `image()`) so it matches your art's real proportions — a tall character squashed into a square looks wrong.
Give an `ImageSprite` decoration a velocity so it drifts across the scene.
Replace your collectibles with image sprites too — but remember they need `extends Blob` if the player has to collect them.
challenge: Fake an animation: load **two** `PImage` fields and swap between them based on a frame counter. That is the whole idea behind Bonus Lesson C, and you will have discovered it yourself.
flintHint: Good things to ask: "my image shows up as a white box", "Processing says it cannot load my image", or "how do I make my picture the right size?" Tell it your file name and where you put it.
wrapup: Why can't you use `collidesWith()` on an `ImageSprite`? What do you do instead if you want an image character with collision detection?
assignmentTask: Put your own art into your sketch — as decoration, as your character, or both.
assignmentDo: Get at least one image file loading from your `data/` folder.
If you want your character to be an image, put a `PImage` inside an `extends Blob` class so collisions still work.
Size everything so it looks intentional, not stretched.
submit: Your sketch folder, zipped — **including the `data/` folder**, or your images will be missing and nothing will run.
A screenshot of your sketch with your art in it.
Your answer to **Show your thinking** below.

Put a `PImage` inside an `extends Blob` character.
Explain why an `ImageSprite` cannot collide, and what to do instead.
standard: Add images via the `data/` folder, display decorations with `ImageSprite`, and use a `PImage` inside an `extends Blob` character so collisions still work.

stages.name: Getting Started
stages.text: My image draws as a blank or colored box, or not at all. **Next step:** make sure the file is in the sketch's `data/` folder (Sketch → Show Sketch Folder) and the filename matches **exactly**. A white box usually means the PNG has no transparency.

stages.name: Got It Working
stages.text: My own image appears in the sketch — as an `ImageSprite` decoration and/or as my character.

stages.name: Made It Mine
stages.text: …and I themed the look with my own art — a character image plus decorations (or a background image), sized to fit.

stages.name: Went Beyond
stages.text: …and I used an image **inside** an `extends Blob` character so collisions still work, added drifting image decorations, or swapped between two images to fake animation.

thinking: In one or two sentences: why does a picture-character still need to `extends Blob`?

di.h: The data/ folder — do this together, slowly
p: **Sketch → Show Sketch Folder**, create a folder named `data`, drag an image in. Processing finds it automatically when the sketch runs.
This is the number one setup hurdle in the lesson. Walk through it on the projector and then wait until every student has actually done it before moving on.
Supported: PNG, JPG, GIF. Recommend PNG for the transparency.
Three constructor forms: default 100×100, one number for a square, two numbers for width and height.
It has all the familiar methods: `move()`, `setVelocity()`, `followMouse()`, `drawSprite()`.
**It does not have `collidesWith()`.** Scenery only. Say this now, because it is the whole point of the second half of the lesson.

di.h: Image inside an extends Blob character
p: Store a `PImage` field, load it in the constructor with `p.loadImage(fileName)`, and in `drawSprite()` use `pushStyle()` / `imageMode(CENTER)` / `image()` / `popStyle()`.
The Blob's radius is still the invisible collision circle. The picture is only what you see.
This is the right approach whenever a thing needs **both** a picture and collisions — which is every player, collectible, and hazard.
PNG files can have transparent backgrounds, but only if they were saved that way. A PNG without transparency draws a white or colored rectangle behind the art, and this surprises students every time.
remove.bg is a free tool that strips backgrounds if a student is stuck with a bad file.

guided: Before class if possible: have students find or draw a small PNG. Options: a free sprite from opengameart.org, or a 32×32 character drawn in any paint program. Drawing their own is better if you have the time.
Everyone opens **Sketch → Show Sketch Folder** and creates the `data` folder together. Wait for everyone.
Everyone drags in their image and reads the filename out loud, exactly, including capitals.
**Do the `ImageSprite` decoration first.** It is the simpler pattern and it gets a picture on screen within minutes, which is the motivating moment.
Debug the inevitable white boxes and not-found errors as a group — the two causes are filename mismatch and missing transparency.
Then introduce the image-inside-a-Blob pattern for their character, so collisions still work.
Release for personalization: background images, more decorations, sizing.
pitfalls: **No `data/` folder, or it is misnamed** (`Data`, `datas`, or created in the wrong directory). The single biggest time sink.
**Filename typos**, including the extension and capitalisation. `Hero.PNG` is not `hero.png`.
**PNG without transparency** → a white rectangle around the character. Looks like a code bug; is not.
**Forgetting `imageMode(CENTER)`** → art offset down and right from the hitbox, so collisions feel broken.
Trying `collidesWith()` on an `ImageSprite`. It will not compile, and the error will not explain why.
**Zipping the sketch without the `data/` folder** when submitting, so nothing runs. Say this out loud at collection time.
Huge source images (2000×2000) scaled to 60×60 — works, but slow and blurry. Small source art is better.
teacher.wrapupAnswer: `ImageSprite` is not a `Blob`, so it has no `collidesWith()`. For a character that needs both a picture and collisions, put a `PImage` inside a class that `extends Blob`.
notes: This is enrichment. Nothing in the capstone requires it, and a student who skips it is not blocked.
The radius in `super()` is the hitbox and does not need to match the image exactly. A radius **slightly smaller** than the visible art feels fairer to play.
`ImageSprite` also has `setRotation(angle)` and `rotate(amount)` in radians — great for spinning decorations. Mention only if asked.
Fast finishers: two `PImage` fields toggled on a frame counter to fake animation. That is a natural bridge into Bonus Lesson C.
Sourcing art can eat the whole period. Have a small folder of ready-to-use PNGs available for students who cannot decide.
